correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge5\), distinct roots at the inclusive Euclidean scale \(\sqrt2\) are adjacent exactly when their inner product is one. The signed-support pairwise-intersection classification gives \(2n\) star complexes each homeomorphic to \(S^{n-2}\), with single-vertex pair intersections and no triple intersections, plus precisely \(8\binom n3\) nonstar two-simplices. Replacing pairwise point gluings by intervals, collapsing embedded trees inside the simply connected stars, and null-homotoping their boundary arcs identifies the complete Rips complex with \(\mathcal O_n^{(2)}\vee\bigvee^{2n}S^{n-2}\). The crosspolytope two-skeleton has second Betti rank \(8\binom n3-2n(n-1)+2n-1\), is simply connected, and is a wedge of two-spheres. The standalone verifier exhaustively enumerates the finite cases \(n=4,5,6,7\) and their mod-two boundary ranks, corroborating the all-rank integral proof rather than replacing it.

originality.rationale: The claimed Euclidean type-\(D_n\) root-set Rips homotopy type for \(n\ge5\), containing \(2n\) sphere summands in degree \(n-2\) alongside independent degree-two summands, was not located among relevant indexed research records or the inspected published comparisons. The rank-four special case does not imply the uniform higher-rank theorem. The closest line-graph theorem addresses a strict supergraph of the root adjacency graph, and Green treats different half-cube vertices. Search absence is not a global novelty proof, and bibliographic risks remain.

value.rationale: The canonical type-\(D_n\) root set has a first nontrivial Euclidean Rips threshold at \(\sqrt2\). For all \(n\ge5\), the theorem gives a motivated infinite-family mixed-dimensional *integral homotopy* decomposition: \(2n\) high-degree spheres arise from signed-coordinate stars, while the two-skeleton of a crosspolytope contributes \(8\binom n3-2n(n-1)+2n-1\) independent two-spheres. Ordinary Betti-number tables do not explain the splitting, and the nonzero higher homology distinguishes the root graph from the complete-multipartite line-graph case. No claim is made about later scales or symmetry modules.
